SECTION VII - THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL SHORT TERM USES OF MAN'S ENVIRONMENT AND THE MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF LONG TERM PRODUCTIVITY
7.01 The Rio Grande is a natural water resource which is important in maintaining and improving the living standards and life's amenities for the people of south Texas. Depending on changing trends and future need, the proposed action can have good or bad effects on the region or State. These net effects involve short-term localized environmental losses that are traded off for more long-term regional benefits to be gained. Implementation of the proposed plan would result in some adverse impacts to the biotic productivity on the lands committed to facility development. Once the project is operational, it will require commitments of manpower and dollars for operation and maintenance throughout the life of the project. Long-term benefits to be gained from the project at the expense of the short-term environmental losses include the electric power and energy to meet present load demands without utilization of fossil fuels, and a regional economic and social stability resulting from the increased efficiency of the existing power network.
